market_summary: The pre-market setup is mixed and wait-and-see, based on 1524 articles from Yahoo Finance, TradingView, Seeking Alpha, Investing.com, CNBC Markets. The dominant theme is macro, with 649 macro items, 478 company items, 343 industry items, and 54 policy items. The tape looks more useful for identifying near-term rotation and risk appetite than for making a single directional index call.
macro_summary: Late Cycle Markets are balancing easier policy expectations against growth and earnings risk, keeping leadership narrow and confirmation dependent. The market is taking its direction from oil/energy, with investors testing whether policy support can offset slower growth and earnings risk. Macro coverage is concentrated around oil/energy (120), Fed/rates (111), inflation (108), growth/jobs (29). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_summary: Sentiment is mixed and wait-and-see: 201 positive, 185 negative, and 1138 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.
